A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FedGR research, retaining the central method and benchmarks. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Clothing1M experiments, component ablations, and memorization analyses in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds baseline results, sensitivity studies, memorization experiments and supplementary evaluation results.

M1.justification: The global-model loss sieving, conditional label refinement, revised EMA distillation and representation regularization remain. Centralized Sieving becomes Federated Sieving, and sniffing-then-refining becomes sieving-and-refining. Explicit identifiers, cached EMA predictions and pseudocode expand the documentation without establishing a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate image classification on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100 and Clothing1M, covering IID/non-IID partitions and synthetic or natural label noise. The additional memorization experiments reuse already represented datasets and noise conditions; their client counts and evaluation procedures change settings rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: FedDiv, cited but not evaluated in v1, becomes an evaluated comparator in v2 Tables 1–3 on all three benchmarks. The other comparator memberships are retained, including the absence of FedNoRo from the Clothing1M comparison.

E3.justification: Clothing1M's reported learning rate changes from 0.003 to 0.01 and local epochs from 10 to 2. v2 adds best-round accuracy evaluation alongside the retained last-ten-round mean, and observation experiments with 20/100 clients and 50%/80% noise. Corresponding client-level observation captions also change the stated noise type from Mixed to Sym; this establishes a reported setting revision, not necessarily reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and strong-augmentation ablations, v2 adds weak-augmentation removal, online EMA distillation and warm-up sampling controls, plus sensitivity tests for four regularization/EMA hyperparameters. It also expands memorization analyses, examines evaluation-metric sensitivity, adds Clothing1M learning curves, and visualizes clean/noisy loss separation in Figure 22.

E5.justification: v1 Appendix A.2 reports Clothing1M using seed 1 alone; v2 Appendix A.5 specifies seeds 1, 13 and 42, and Table 3 adds mean and standard deviation. The three-seed reporting practice for the CIFAR benchmark experiments is retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial baseline, sensitivity, best-round and observation results. FedDiv changes some rankings: CIFAR-10 IID asymmetric noise with phi=1 gives 92.86 versus FedGR's retained 91.64. Clothing1M results are replaced under revised settings, including FedGR IID 70.26 becoming 71.19±0.42. Table 4's non-IID symmetric-noise FedGR entry changes from 64.24±5.10 to 63.64±5.39.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.7 introduces smoothness, stochastic-variance, heterogeneity and regularizer-gradient assumptions, a descent lemma, and a theorem with proof sketches claiming FedAvg-like convergence. v1 contains method equations and complexity accounting but no corresponding convergence analysis. Complexity accounting is also revised, including FedGR's forward cost from (e+2)F to (E+3)F.

C1.justification: The central observation and FedGR robustness contribution remain. v2 adds a convergence guarantee to the advertised contributions and strengthens performance wording from success in almost all settings to consistent superiority. These extend the claims without redefining the central research contribution; the categorical superiority wording has exceptions in the tables.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations involving cancellation of noisy client updates, implicit early stopping, and conflicts between global robustness and local adaptation. It qualifies the observation at high noise, discusses Clothing1M's shared-noise-pattern limitation, and expands privacy reasoning. Conversely, v1's explicit limitations concerning dynamic participation and fairness disappear rather than moving elsewhere.

D1.justification: v2 adds server/client pseudocode, explicit sample-identifier exchanges, cached teacher-output details, FedDiv implementation information and settings for new observation experiments. It revises Clothing1M hyperparameters and reports RTX 3090 rather than RTX 4090 hardware. Code release is newly promised, but neither PDF supplies accessible experimental code.

R1.justification: v2 substantially revises positioning around the closest prior observation: Appendix A.3 explicitly discusses Kim et al.'s FLR and distinguishes broader validation and comparison with centralized training. It also expands the cited literature with works including FedClean, EMA analyses and augmentation studies, while removing several earlier references.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and method explanations are extensively rewritten. v2 adds a method overview, renames modules, reorganizes experimental reporting, and restructures the appendix into notation, observations, supplementary results, implementation, privacy, theory, complexity and visualization sections. An impact statement is added.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is completely redrawn, the separate EMA-update diagram disappears, and the F-score display changes from violins to boxplots. Main result tables place IID/non-IID conditions side by side and add average columns and ranking shading. New tables and plots accompany the analyses; retained data-partition figures are enlarged and relocated.

improvement.justification: The added controls, parameter sensitivity tests, best-round checks, three-seed Clothing1M reporting and explicit algorithms improve empirical scrutiny and reproducibility. These gains are tempered by new reliability problems: Appendix A.7's displayed bound retains a nonvanishing noise term despite the advertised convergence rate, and blanket superiority wording conflicts with FedDiv results. Removing the earlier participation and fairness limitations also reduces transparency.
